findings.text: follow-on, non-blocking: the new byte runner passes capture_output=True, so velocity.git over it now captures git's stderr where subprocess.check_output previously left it inherited on the process's stderr. On the success path any git warning that used to reach the operator is now silently held; on the failure path the behaviour improves (CalledProcessError.stderr is populated where check_output left it None). The new test test_git_failure_returns_bytes_and_checked_wrappers_keep_their_error_domains asserts the capture deliberately and the section's own prose does not name the change, so this is a recorded behaviour change rather than a defect.

justifications.durability: tests/test_one_cache_cascade_serves_every_kind.py pins each of the five kinds' directory across default, isolated home, XDG, both and configured environments (25 cells), the override precedence, the unknown-kind refusal, the single XDG_CACHE_HOME owner by AST, the git error domains of run_git/git/routing._git, the single subprocess-invoking function, and the velocity-imports-no-crew layering; the negative control (private cascade restored in capabilities.py) reddens the parity cells, the owner test and the ledger/detector test, so the guard is shown to fire.
justifications.evidence: base-gate.log 475 passed in 366.25s EXIT=0 and final-gate.log 519 passed in 365.43s EXIT=0, both against a declared revision and tree with module=_store.py and cwd named; the negative-gate.log ends 7 failed, 37 passed, EXIT=1; head-measurements.json records public_definitions 1476 -> 1477, the single cache owner and the single velocity process owner; added_failure_count 0 was derived from the two gate logs by review.added_failures_from_gate_logs, not asserted from the manifest. One point withheld: the after gate ran at the source head 6eb681901 while the reviewed head is the docs commit 3184f4a8b, so the run and the delivered revision differ by one evidence-only commit.
justifications.fit: cache_root lands in the path-helpers section of reckon/_store.py beside _config_home, the package's owner of RECKON_HOME precedence, reading the home through it and keeping each kind's leaf, env var and home-order in the table as §13 argues; run_git stays on velocity where §10 placed the public git names, with the generic runner's placement tradeoff already recorded by the plan-design review; the mode wrappers state their contract (git raises on bytes, routing._git translates to CrewError, the raw runner returns the process); no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family was added.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The section's two deliverables are both the working tree's behaviour at the reviewed head: grep 'def cache_root' returns one line in reckon/_store.py, the sole XDG_CACHE_HOME reading is that function, velocity.py's sole subprocess-invoking function is run_git, routing._git contains no subprocess call, pick_input_cache_root is gone with every caller rewired, and the 25 base-recorded directory cells are preserved by the shared cascade.
justifications.reuse: This section is de-duplication end to end: five cache resolvers in two orders plus the detector's copy collapse to one kind-keyed function, and four velocity subprocess sites plus routing's private runner collapse to one byte runner. No new fork is introduced — the kind table is data, the reviewers' contracts are preserved by thin mode wrappers, and the residual second runner (the detector's _git) is outside this section and named by §12 and the git-access-has-one-owner followup.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every path in the base..head diff is inside the declared write paths and every change serves §13's two mechanisms; nothing touches the shared plan, project index or sprint state, and the deliberately out-of-scope direct git invocations across the twenty-one modules are left to the followup the section names.
